transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, uh, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time today. It's probably nothing too serious, to be honest, but... well, what brings me in is that ever since I stopped working, I just can’t seem to slow down. 

I'm constantly up and moving from one little job around the house to the next, all day long. It's almost like I still have a work crew waiting on me to get things moving, you know? I mean, staying active at my age is a good thing, right? I just like to be productive... but I guess it's getting to be a bit much, and I just wanted to see if that's normal. Am I explaining that alright?
Do you feel like you have to do these tasks around the house, or is it something you just want to do?

Well, gosh, that's a good question. I, uh... I don't know if "have to" is the right way to put it. I definitely don't want you to think I'm, you know, obsessing over things or acting crazy or anything like that. 

I guess it's more that I just... want to be useful? Like, I'll see a loose cabinet hinge or notice the garage needs sweeping, and I just figure I might as well get right to it. It just feels better to keep busy rather than sitting around. That's a normal way to look at it, isn't it? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Do you feel anxious or uncomfortable when you're not busy with these tasks?

Anxious? Oh, no, I wouldn't say anxious. I definitely don't want to give you the impression that I'm a nervous wreck or anything like that! I'm a pretty upbeat guy. 

But, uh... I guess "uncomfortable" might be a fair word for it. Like, if I have to just sit still for a long stretch... say, if I'm sitting through a quiet meeting or listening to a talk at church. I just sort of... well, I feel like I've got to shift around in my seat a lot. Or I'll catch myself tapping my foot. Sometimes I just get this strong urge to get up and stretch my legs, even when I know darn well I should just stay put and be polite. 

It's nothing major, really, just a little extra physical energy, you know? I always try my best not to bother the folks sitting next to me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill here.
Has your need to stay busy and keep moving caused any problems with your relationships with family or friends?

Well, I... I wouldn't say "problems," exactly. I definitely don't want to make it sound like I'm a burden on my family or a bad friend. I try really hard to be dependable, I really do. 

But, um, I suppose my wife has had to step in a bit more lately. She's so wonderful, she really is... but she's sort of had to take over keeping our calendar. And, well, she checks behind me sometimes on things I've started but maybe got distracted from. I feel awful making extra work for her, but she says she doesn't mind. 

And, uh, with my friends... well, I've had to apologize to the folks at the community center and my garden group a few times. I'll promise to help with something or show up for a project, and then I just... I get caught up in moving around doing other things and completely forget, or I double-book myself. I hate letting people down, and I always make sure to apologize right away. I hope they know I don't do it on purpose. Does that sound like the kind of thing you were asking about? I really hope I'm not painting too terrible a picture of myself here.
Do you ever find yourself thinking about a task or problem over and over again, even when you're not actively working on it?

Oh, no, not really. I mean, I definitely don't want you to think I'm the sort of person who gets stuck in their own head or, you know, obsesses over things. I'm usually pretty good at just moving on to the next thing! 

I guess sometimes if I'm trying to fix something in the garage and it's being stubborn, I might mull it over a bit while I'm eating lunch, just trying to figure out the right tool to use. But it's nothing that keeps me up at night or bothers me. Once a job is done, or if I just need to put it down for the day, I can usually just let it go. I like to keep a clear head, you know? I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for. I just wouldn't say I get stuck on things over and over.
Do you find yourself mentally replaying conversations or events from the day after they've happened?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I do that. I mean, I certainly don't want you to think I sit around dwelling on the past or second-guessing myself all the time! I try to be the kind of person who just takes things as they come and leaves the past in the past. 

Sure, if I had a really nice chat with my neighbor or a good laugh with my grandkids, I might smile about it later on. But replaying things? No, not really. Once a conversation is over, I'm usually just looking forward to whatever's next on the agenda. I try to keep things positive and moving forward, you know? 

I hope that makes sense. Am I answering these questions okay for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you feel guilty when you're not being productive or active?

Well, I... I wouldn't say "guilty," exactly. I mean, I definitely don't want to sound like I'm beating myself up or anything like that. I try to be gentle with myself, I really do. 

I guess I just... I like to be useful, you know? So if I'm just sitting in my recliner for too long, I might feel a little itch to go check on the tomatoes or sweep the porch. But it's not a bad feeling, really! Just a preference for staying busy. I certainly don't sit around feeling bad about myself if I take a breather. I think it's important to relax sometimes, don't you? 

I hope that's the right kind of answer. I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound like I have a problem with resting, because I really don't! Am I doing okay with these questions?
Do you often find your mind preoccupied with thoughts, even when you're not actively trying to think about something?

Oh, gosh, no, I wouldn't say my mind is preoccupied like that. I mean, I definitely don't want you to get the impression that my head is just spinning all the time with random thoughts. I try to stay pretty grounded, you know?

I suppose everyone daydreams a little bit here and there, like maybe wondering what the weather will be like tomorrow or thinking about what to make for dinner. But my mind doesn't just run away with me when I'm trying to relax. If I'm sitting on the porch watching the birds, I'm just watching the birds! I don't have a bunch of noise going on up there. I like a peaceful mind. 

I hope that's helpful for you. I just wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting around lost in my own head all day. Is that the sort of thing you were wondering about?
Do you feel restless if you are not engaged in some kind of physical or mental activity?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I feel restless. I mean, I certainly don't want to give the impression that I can't sit still or that I'm always pacing around the house or anything like that! I'm pretty good at just taking it easy.

Sure, I like to putter around the garage or do a crossword puzzle, but if I'm just sitting and watching a little television, I'm perfectly content. I don't get that antsy feeling where I just have to get up and do something. I think at my age, it's nice to just enjoy the quiet moments, you know? I try to be the kind of person who can just go with the flow.

I hope that answers your question alright. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I spend my days. Am I doing okay so far?
Do you think you would feel bored if you weren't constantly doing something?

Oh, well... no, I really wouldn't say I get bored. I don't want you to think I need to be entertained every second of the day, like a little kid or something! I'm perfectly fine just sitting quietly. 

I mean, I do enjoy my little projects, like fixing up things around the house or keeping the yard looking nice. But if I don't have anything on the agenda for the afternoon, I don't sit there twiddling my thumbs and feeling miserable about it. I can just enjoy a cup of coffee on the porch without needing some big activity to keep me occupied. I think I'm pretty easy to please in that regard.

I hope I'm explaining that right. I just wouldn't want you to think I'm the sort of person who can't handle a little downtime. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like you can relax and unwind when you're not doing something active?

Oh, absolutely. Yes, I can relax just fine. I definitely don't want you to think I'm one of those folks who is always wound up tight as a drum. I think it's so important to be able to just... unwind, you know? 

When the day is done, I'm perfectly happy to just kick my shoes off and settle into my recliner. I don't feel like I have a motor running inside me that won't shut off. I can just watch the evening news and let the day go. I really try to keep things low-stress and easygoing. 

I hope that's what you were looking for. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea about how I handle my evenings. Is that the kind of thing you needed to know?
Do you feel like you're able to stop an activity when you want to, or do you find it difficult to stop once you've started?

Oh, I can stop just fine. I definitely don't have any trouble with that. I wouldn't want you to think I'm stubborn or get, you know, overly fixated on my little projects! 

If I'm working on a crossword or out in the yard, and it's time to come in for supper or run an errand, I just put it down. It's really no bother at all. I try to be very agreeable about that sort of thing. I know some folks get so wrapped up in what they're doing that they can't tear themselves away, but I'm not like that. I can always pick it back up the next day, right? 

I hope that's the kind of detail you're looking for. Am I giving you what you need to know?
Do you feel like you must always be doing something because you cannot tolerate just being idle?

Oh, no, not at all. I really don't mind being idle sometimes. I wouldn't want you to think I'm... well, that I'm one of those people who just can't sit still or who always has to be busy, busy, busy. 

I think it's perfectly fine to just sit and enjoy the quiet. Like I said, I can sit on the porch and just watch the world go by. I don't get antsy or feel like I'm wasting time or anything like that. I'm very comfortable just letting a quiet afternoon be a quiet afternoon. 

I try to be pretty easygoing about my time. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and answering your questions the right way.
Do you feel like you're doing things to avoid feeling unproductive, rather than because you genuinely enjoy the activities themselves?

Oh, goodness, no. I really do enjoy the things I spend my time on. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just... well, spinning my wheels or doing busywork just to prove I'm useful. 

Since I'm not working anymore, I just stick to the things I genuinely like doing, you know? Whether it's tinkering a bit in the garage or just tending to the yard, I do it because I like it. I don't feel guilty about taking it easy, so I don't force myself to be productive if I don't want to be. I just like to enjoy my days as they come. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right for you. I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture.
Do you think you would feel uneasy or dissatisfied if you had an entire day with absolutely no tasks or responsibilities?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. A whole day with nothing to do sounds... well, it sounds quite lovely, actually. I wouldn't want you to think I'm one of those restless types who can't handle a bit of peace and quiet. 

I'm perfectly content to just take the day as it comes. If there are no chores or errands, I'm more than happy to just relax, maybe read a bit or watch a program. I don't get all tied up in knots feeling like I ought to be doing something important. I think at my age, you earn the right to just have a quiet day, don't you think? 

I really try to just go with the flow. I hope that's an alright answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you think you could spend a whole day doing absolutely nothing without feeling the need to get up and do something?

Oh, absolutely. I could easily spend a whole day just doing nothing at all. I really don't have that... that urge to constantly be up and about, you know? 

I wouldn't want you to get the wrong idea, like I'm bouncing off the walls or anything. I can just sit in my favorite chair, maybe listen to the radio or just watch the birds outside, and I'm perfectly happy. I don't get that itchy feeling where I just have to jump up and find a project. I'm very comfortable just letting the day pass by quietly. 

I really do enjoy a peaceful day without any fuss. I hope that's the kind of thing you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the way you need me to.
Do you feel like you are driven to keep moving and doing things because you are trying to avoid feeling restless or uncomfortable when you are not active?

Oh, no, definitely not. I wouldn't say I'm driven like that at all. I really don't have that uncomfortable, restless feeling you're describing. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just pacing the floors or keeping busy because I can't stand to sit still. 

I just move around when there's something that needs doing, or if it's something I want to do. If I'm sitting down and relaxing, I'm genuinely just relaxing. I don't have this... this nervous energy forcing me to get up. I'm very much at ease when I'm not active. 

I hope I'm being clear enough about that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right impression of how I spend my time.
Do you think keeping busy helps you avoid feeling sad or down?

Oh, goodness, no. I wouldn't say that at all. I'm really a pretty cheerful fellow, most of the time. I don't really get those... well, those sad or down feelings you're mentioning. 

I wouldn't want you to worry that I'm depressed or anything like that. If I happen to be doing a few things around the house, it's just normal day-to-day stuff, not because I'm trying to chase away the blues or hide from bad thoughts. I'm genuinely quite content with my life just the way it is. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you exactly the kind of information you need from me.
Do you think keeping busy is a way for you to avoid dealing with difficult emotions or thoughts?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I really don't have too many difficult thoughts to run away from, to be honest. I'm a pretty straightforward guy. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm bottling things up or... or hiding from my feelings by tinkering in the garage or whatever. I just do things because they need doing, or because I enjoy them. I don't really have any dark clouds hanging over me that I'm trying to outrun. 

I'm pretty comfortable in my own head, really. I hope that's alright? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and answering your questions properly.
Do you find that you have difficulty sustaining focus on a single task for an extended period?

Oh, well... no, I wouldn't really say I have difficulty focusing. Not in any way that causes a problem, anyway. I mean, at my age, I think it's pretty normal to maybe hop from one little chore to another, right? 

I wouldn't want you to think my mind is just wandering all over the place or that I can't finish what I start. If I'm doing something important, I can certainly stick with it. Sometimes I just... well, I might decide to switch gears and do something else for a bit. It's more of a choice, really, just keeping things varied. 

I'm doing okay with all that, I think. I hope that's the sort of answer you were looking for? I'm just trying to give you the best picture of how things are for me.
